questions.q: Where was Jim when he woke up in the coracle?
choices: Off the south-west end of Treasure Island
Deep inside the North Inlet near the shore
Close beside the beach below the stockade
Right next to the rocks of Skeleton Island
questions.evidence: found myself tossing at the south-west end of Treasure Island

questions.q: Why did Jim decide not to land near Haulbowline Head?
choices: Breakers on the rocks could dash him to death
Pirates were camped on the beach right below it
The tide had gone out and left no water there
His paddle had broken and he could not steer
questions.evidence: dashed to death upon the rough shore

questions.q: What were the "huge slimy monsters" Jim saw on the rocks?
choices: Harmless sea lions
Giant sea snails
A pack of sharks
Huge crocodiles
questions.evidence: they were sea lions, and entirely harmless

questions.q: Jim fears "spending my strength in vain to scale the beetling crags." What are beetling crags?
choices: Steep, overhanging cliffs
Piles of loose, dry sand
Swarms of buzzing insects
Thick, tangled woods

questions.q: What did Jim remember Silver saying that helped him decide where to go?
choices: A current runs northward along the west coast
The wind always blows from the north at night
The south shore is the safest place to land
Sea lions on the rocks guard Flint's treasure
questions.evidence: the current that sets northward along the whole west coast

questions.q: Which place did Jim hope to land on instead?
choices: The Cape of the Woods
The point of Haulbowline Head
The foot of Mizzen-mast Hill
Captain Kidd's old anchorage
questions.evidence: reserve my strength for an attempt to land upon the kindlier-looking Cape of the Woods

questions.q: What happened when Jim first sat up to try paddling?
choices: The coracle ran down a wave and plunged its nose into the next
He paddled hard and went straight toward the shore at last
A wave tore the paddle out of his hands and carried it off
The coracle flipped right over and threw him into the sea
questions.evidence: struck her nose, with a spout of spray, deep into the side of the next wave

questions.q: What did Jim use to bail the water out of the coracle?
choices: His sea-cap
A small tin cup
One of his shoes
His bare hands
questions.evidence: baled out the coracle with my sea-cap

questions.q: What did Jim learn about how the coracle moved through the waves?
choices: Left alone, it found the low places between the steep waves
It only stayed afloat as long as he paddled very hard
It rode the waves best when he stood up in the middle
It moved fastest when he pointed it against the current
questions.evidence: threaded, so to speak, her way through these lower parts

questions.q: What began to torture Jim as he drew near the trees?
choices: Thirst
Cold
A cut leg
Sunburn
questions.evidence: I now began to be tortured with thirst

questions.q: What did Jim suddenly see not half a mile in front of him?
choices: The HISPANIOLA under sail
A boat crowded with pirates
Ben Gunn rowing toward him
Captain Flint's old wreck
questions.evidence: I beheld the HISPANIOLA under sail

questions.q: Why did the HISPANIOLA keep turning into the wind and stopping with flapping sails?
choices: Nobody was steering her
The pirates were chasing Jim
Her main mast had snapped
She was stuck on a sandbank
questions.evidence: It became plain to me that nobody was steering

questions.q: What did Jim hope he might do if he could get on board the schooner?
choices: Return the ship to her captain
Sail all the way home to England
Join the pirates and share the gold
Search the cabin for the treasure map
questions.evidence: I might return the vessel to her captain

questions.q: What thought "doubled" Jim's courage as he chased the ship?
choices: The water breaker on board
The treasure in the ship's hold
Captain Smollett's words of praise
The loaded pistols in the cabin
questions.evidence: the thought of the water breaker beside the fore companion doubled my growing courage

questions.q: How did Jim finally get onto the HISPANIOLA?
choices: He leaped up and caught the jib-boom as the ship struck the coracle
He climbed up a rope ladder hanging over the side of the ship
He swam to the bow and pulled himself up the anchor chain
Israel Hands leaned over the rail and pulled him aboard by the arm
questions.evidence: With one hand I caught the jib-boom

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Jim drifts in the coracle, then chases and boards the drifting HISPANIOLA
Jim paddles back to the stockade and helps fight off another pirate attack
Jim lands on the island and finds Flint's treasure hidden in a cave
Jim is spotted by Long John Silver and captured on the western beach
questions.evidence: I was left without retreat on the HISPANIOLA
